newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin attacks French towns' child curfews.
newsitem.headline: Jospin attacks French towns' child curfews.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on Friday criticised midnight curfews for children in some towns, saying they were a misguided way of combating crime by the very young.
Conservative municipalities in Dreux and Gien, west of Paris, Sorgues in southern France and Aulnay in the Paris suburbs have ordered the controversial curfews this summer for children under 13.
"We can't resolve this sort of problem with this type of curfew, which recalls other eras," Socialist Jospin told Radio Luxembourg.
"Naturally, no one thinks that children should be out wandering the streets after midnight at the age of 12 or less," Jospin said, adding there was a problem with juvenile delinquency in France.

"So these problems should not be treated lightly," he said. The midnight curfews are aimed at countering vandalism during the school holidays, especially by footloose children living in grim high-rise blocks.

Jospin said families should take more responsibility. "We should perhaps resolve (the problems) more with educators, with social contacts, social workers, than by hauling 12-year-old children off to police stations," he said.
Junior Schools Minister Segolene Royal said last week that the curfews reduced children to the status of stray dogs.
